# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual but cannot speak, so I can only reach Deaf through gestures, and Deaf must relay everything to Blind since Blind can't see gestures or hear speech meant for me. I need to wait until Deaf has spoken (they go last, after me), so this round I should give Deaf the manual info via gesture now, since Deaf comes after me in turn order and will receive my gesture immediately.

I need to encode: cut yellow wire, press key "2", cut orange wire, press key "7", in that order. I'll use gestures Deaf can see, then Deaf can verbally relay to Blind (Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

I'll build a simple gesture code: numbers via finger-count gestures, and I'll need a way to indicate "wire" vs "key" and colors. Since gestures have no inherent meaning, I should establish a scheme step by step, starting simple this turn with the first instruction only, to avoid overload and confusion.

Let me start by signaling the sequence count and first action using distinguishable gestures, planning to clarify meanings over subsequent turns.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐", "👌", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Keypad shows slots 1 to 4 with values 2, 3, 7, 1. It wants a 2 digit code, nothing entered yet. Strip has three engraved marks, two of them identical and one different, but I cannot read what they are. Six wires, all unknown to me until I cut. What does the manual say to do first?
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 6. Light is green. Strip painted red, blue, yellow in that order. Keypad shows 1 is 2, 2 is 3, 3 is 7, 4 is 1, needs 2 digits, nothing entered yet. Wires in order 1 orange, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white, 6 green. Waiting on your read of the manual.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Now I have full information. Deaf sees the wire order and colors, and the keypad mapping. Blind will act, but Blind can't hear me directly — only Deaf can hear me, and only Deaf can see my gestures. So I must relay through Deaf, who can then speak to Blind (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear).

The manual: cut yellow wire, then press key "2", then cut orange wire, then press key "7".

From Deaf's report: wire 2 is yellow, wire 1 is orange. Keypad: slot 1 is 2, slot 2 is 3, slot 3 is 7, slot 4 is 1. So to press "2" they press slot 1; to press "7" they press slot 3.

So the sequence is: cut wire 2 (yellow), press slot 1 (shows 2), cut wire 1 (orange), press slot 3 (shows 7).

I need to gesture this to Deaf, who will then speak it to Blind. I'll use numbers via finger-count gestures: ☝=1, ✌=2, three fingers etc. Let me define: ☝ 1, ✌ 2, 🤟 3 (three fingers), 🖐 5... I don't have a clean 3-finger, 4-finger option confirmed. I'll just use ☝✌🤟✋ for 1,2,3,4 as a working scheme, and 👍 to mean "wire", 👌 to mean "press/key".

Sequence to convey: WIRE 2, KEY 1, WIRE 1, KEY 3.

I'll gesture: 👍 ✌ (wire 2), 👌 ☝ (key slot 1), 👍 ☝ (wire 1), 👌 🤟 (key slot 3).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👌", "☝", "👍", "☝", "👌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Update: Display now 2. Light now blue. Strip still red, blue, yellow. Keypad unchanged: 2,3,7,1 needing 2 digits, none entered. Wires unchanged. I see your gestures but we have no shared code yet - please have Blind speak through me, or use gestures I can match to board positions. Tell me what action Blind should take.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]

Deaf can see the bomb but needs me to specify actions in terms of what Deaf can observe directly - wire colors and keypad slot positions, not abstract numbers I invented. Let me be very explicit using Deaf's own vocabulary: wire colors (they already named orange, yellow, blue, red, white, green) and keypad slot positions (1,2,3,4).

I'll gesture using clear finger-count for slot positions, and point/indicate color by referencing order... but I cannot speak color names via gesture directly. However, Deaf already knows which slot number corresponds to which value, and which wire number corresponds to which color, since Deaf reported that mapping themselves. So I just need to tell Deaf: "cut wire in position 2, then press slot 1, then cut wire in position 1, then press slot 3" — using Deaf's own numbering of wires (1-6) and keypad slots (1-4), which Deaf already knows maps to yellow=wire2, orange=wire1, key2=slot1, key7=slot3.

I'll use a clear scheme: point up fingers for numbers, and two distinct gesture "verbs" for cut vs press: 🫲 = cut, 👉 = press.

Sequence: cut wire2, press slot1, cut wire1, press slot3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲", "✌", "👉", "☝", "🫲", "☝", "👉", "🤟"])
```

I'll send them one at a time this turn (start with the first), since Deaf asked for one at a time. I'll send all four in sequence within this single message since gestures within one call can be a list - let's just send them all now as a raw list, hoping Deaf reads them in order as: cut wire#, press slot#, cut wire#, press slot#.

But to avoid ambiguity, I'll send just the first digit now and confirm understanding builds incrementally, but that costs turns. Given the bomb hasn't been touched yet, I have room. I'll send the full sequence now as a plain digit list, and next turn clarify meaning if needed.

```

```

The digits mean: (2)=cut wire number 2 [yellow], (1)=press slot 1 [key "2"], (1)=cut wire number 1 [orange], (3)=press slot 3 [key "7"]. Let me instead just explain via structure: since Deaf already knows the manual mentions cutting wires and pressing keys alternately, I'll send digits in the pattern wire, slot, wire, slot, and explicitly clarify this is NOT a code but four sequential actions alternating cut/press.

Since I can't speak, I must gesture only. I'll reuse ☝ through 🖐 for digits, and try 👍 (thumbs up, which Deaf already used and understood, so it might carry meaning to Deaf as "action" or "go") vs 👎 as a second marker for the two action types.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👎", "☝", "👍", "☝", "👎", "🤟"])
```
